title: 카페 · 커피
intro: '카페 가기'를 선택하면 자주 가는 카페 묘사 → 카페에 가서 하는 일(루틴) → 카페에서 있었던 기억에 남는 경험 → 예전과 지금의 카페 이용 비교 순서로 출제됩니다. 페르소나는 집 근처 작은 카페에서 아이스 아메리카노를 마시며 과제와 공부를 하는 경영학과 대학생이고, 같은 과 친구 Minji와 자주 함께 갑니다. 카페 하나와 음료 하나만 정해 두면 묘사·루틴·경험·비교가 모두 같은 이야기로 이어집니다.
strategy: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장(Oh, cafes? Sure, let me tell you about my favorite one.) → 기본 정보(어디·얼마나 자주) → 세부(분위기·메뉴·하는 일) → 느낌·이유 → 마무리 문장(So yeah, that's my favorite cafe.)
카페는 '집에서 걸어서 5분 거리의 작은 동네 카페' 하나로 고정하세요. 창가 자리, 조용한 음악, 커피 향 같은 쉬운 디테일 3개면 충분합니다.
루틴은 '수업 끝나고 노트북 들고 카페 → 아이스 아메리카노 주문 → 2~3시간 과제 → 가끔 Minji와 수다' 순서로 시간 흐름을 따라가세요.
비교 질문은 '고등학생 때는 친구들과 수다 떨러 갔다 → 대학생이 된 지금은 공부하러 간다'처럼 목적의 변화를 중심으로 답하면 쉽습니다.

expressions.en: Oh, cafes? Sure, let me tell you about my favorite one.
expressions.ko: 아, 카페요? 네, 제가 제일 좋아하는 곳을 말씀드릴게요.

expressions.en: There's a small cafe about five minutes from my apartment.
expressions.ko: 우리 아파트에서 5분 정도 거리에 작은 카페가 있어요.

expressions.en: I usually order an iced Americano.
I go there two or three times a week.
I like to sit by the window.
I usually do my assignments there.
expressions.note: do my assignments / do my homework

expressions.en: The music is soft, and it smells like coffee.
I often go there with my friend Minji.
It has a really cozy atmosphere.
I can focus better at a cafe than at home.
expressions.ko: 집보다 카페에서 더 집중이 잘 돼요.

expressions.en: I'm kind of a regular there, so the owner knows my order.
expressions.ko: 제가 거기 단골이라서 사장님이 제 주문을 알아요.

expressions.en: When I was in high school, I went to cafes just to hang out.
expressions.ko: 고등학생 때는 그냥 놀려고 카페에 갔어요.

expressions.en: I can't start my day without an iced Americano.
expressions.ko: 아이스 아메리카노 없이는 하루를 시작할 수가 없어요.

expressions.en: It's become my second home, to be honest.
expressions.ko: 솔직히 거긴 제 두 번째 집이 됐어요.

expressions.en: So yeah, that's pretty much why I love that cafe.
expressions.ko: 그러니까 네, 그게 제가 그 카페를 좋아하는 이유예요.
expressions.note: 마무리 문장: So yeah, that's pretty much ~

questions.en: You indicated in the survey that you like going to cafes. Tell me about a cafe you often go to. Where is it, and what does it look like?
questions.ko: 설문에서 카페 가는 것을 좋아한다고 하셨네요. 자주 가는 카페에 대해 말해 주세요. 어디에 있고, 어떻게 생겼나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 위치(집에서 걸어서 5분) → 내부 묘사(창가·조명·음악) → 메뉴 → 좋아하는 이유 → 마무리
small, cozy, quiet, bright 같은 쉬운 형용사로 그림을 그리세요
'I like to sit by the window.'처럼 내가 앉는 자리를 넣으면 생생해져요

answers.IM3: Oh, cafes? Sure, let me tell you about my favorite one. There's a small cafe about five minutes from my apartment. It's on a quiet street in my neighborhood. Inside, there are wooden tables and big windows. I like to sit by the window. The music is soft, and it always smells like coffee. I usually order an iced Americano. It's not expensive, and it tastes great. Yeah, that's my favorite cafe.
answers.IH: Oh, cafes? Sure, let me tell you about my favorite one. There's a small cafe about five minutes from my apartment. It's on a quiet street near the subway station, so I pass by it almost every day. It's not a big chain cafe. It's run by a young couple. Inside, there are about ten wooden tables, some plants, and big windows, so it's really bright during the day. My favorite seat is by the window, because I can watch people walking by. They play soft music, and it always smells like fresh coffee. I usually order an iced Americano, and sometimes I get a piece of cheesecake too. The prices are pretty reasonable for a student like me. It has a really cozy atmosphere. So yeah, that's my favorite cafe.
answers.AL: Oh, cafes? Sure, let me tell you about my favorite one, because I go there way too often. There's a small cafe about five minutes from my apartment, on a quiet little street near the subway station. It's not one of those big chain cafes. It's run by a young couple, and you can tell they really care about the place. When you walk in, the first thing you notice is the smell of fresh coffee. There are about ten wooden tables, lots of green plants, and huge windows, so it's bright and warm during the day. My favorite seat is a corner table by the window. I can plug in my laptop there, and I can watch people walking by when I need a break. They usually play soft acoustic music, so it's never too loud. I almost always order an iced Americano, even in winter, and if I've had a long day, I treat myself to their cheesecake. I'm kind of a regular there now, so the owner knows my order before I even say it. Honestly, it's become my second home. So yeah, that's pretty much why I love that cafe.

questions.en: Why do you go to cafes, and what do you usually do there? Tell me about what you typically do from the moment you arrive until you leave.
questions.ko: 왜 카페에 가고, 거기서 보통 무엇을 하나요? 도착해서 나올 때까지 보통 무엇을 하는지 말해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 언제·얼마나 자주 → 도착해서 주문 → 자리 잡고 과제·공부 → 친구와 수다 → 나올 때 → 마무리
First / Then / After that / When I'm done 으로 순서를 잡으세요
'집보다 카페에서 집중이 잘 된다'는 이유를 한 문장 넣으세요

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about my cafe routine. I go to a cafe two or three times a week, usually after my classes. I go there to study and do my assignments. First, I order an iced Americano. Then I find a seat by the window and open my laptop. I usually study for about two hours. Sometimes my friend Minji comes, and we chat a little. Then I walk home. Yeah, that's my cafe routine.
answers.IH: Okay, let me tell you about my cafe routine. I'm a business student, and I have a lot of assignments, so I go to a cafe two or three times a week to study. I can focus better at a cafe than at home, because at home I just want to lie on my bed. I usually go in the late afternoon, after my classes. First, I order an iced Americano at the counter. Then I find a seat by the window and take out my laptop. I put on my earphones, listen to some ballads, and work on my assignments for about two or three hours. Sometimes my friend Minji joins me, because we're in the same major. We study together, and of course, we chat a lot too. When I'm done, I walk home, which only takes five minutes. So yeah, that's pretty much my cafe routine.
answers.AL: Okay, let me tell you about my cafe routine, because it's a pretty big part of my week. I'm a third-year business student, so I have tons of assignments and team projects, and I go to a cafe two or three times a week to get them done. To be honest, I just can't focus at home. My bed is right next to my desk, and it's way too tempting. So usually in the late afternoon, after my classes, I head to the small cafe near my apartment. First, I order my usual iced Americano. The owner knows me by now, so it's usually ready in a minute. Then I grab my favorite corner seat by the window, plug in my laptop, and put on my earphones. I listen to some soft ballads and work for about two or three hours. Once I get into it, the time just flies by. A lot of the time, my friend Minji joins me, since we're in the same major. We help each other with assignments, but honestly, we end up chatting about everything else too. When I'm finally done, I pack up and walk home, feeling pretty productive. So yeah, that's pretty much how I spend my time at cafes.

questions.en: Tell me about a memorable experience you had at a cafe. What happened, who were you with, and why was it so memorable?
questions.ko: 카페에서 있었던 기억에 남는 경험을 말해 주세요. 무슨 일이 있었고, 누구와 함께였고, 왜 기억에 남나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 언제·누구와(작년 기말고사, Minji) → 무슨 일(커피를 노트북에 쏟음) → 어떻게 해결 → 느낌 → 마무리
과거시제를 유지하세요: was, spilled, panicked, helped
'I'll never forget that day.' 같은 감정 문장 하나가 점수를 올려 줘요

answers.IM3: Oh, let me think. Last year, I was studying for my final exams at my favorite cafe. My friend Minji was with me. Suddenly, I spilled my iced Americano on my laptop! I was so shocked. My notes were on that laptop. Minji and the owner gave me a lot of napkins. Luckily, my laptop was okay. After that, I always keep my drink far from my laptop. Yeah, that was a memorable day.
answers.IH: Oh, let me think. I have a pretty funny story. Last year, during final exams, I was studying at my favorite cafe with my friend Minji. We had a big exam the next day, so we were really stressed out. I was typing my notes on my laptop, and I reached for my iced Americano without looking. Then I knocked it over, right onto my keyboard! I totally panicked, because all my notes for the exam were on that laptop. Minji grabbed some napkins, and the owner ran over with a towel. We turned the laptop off and dried it as fast as we could. Luckily, the next morning, it worked perfectly. Then we did well on the exam too. Now we laugh about it all the time. So yeah, that's my most memorable cafe experience.
answers.AL: Oh, that's a good question. Let me think. Actually, I have a pretty funny story about this. It happened last year, during final exams. My friend Minji and I were studying at my favorite cafe, and we had a really important business exam the next morning. We'd been there for about four hours, so we were tired and totally stressed out. I was typing up my notes on my laptop, and without looking, I reached for my iced Americano. And of course, I knocked it over, right onto my keyboard. For a second, I just froze. All my notes for the exam were on that laptop, and I hadn't backed them up. Minji jumped up and grabbed a whole stack of napkins, and the owner ran over with a towel. We turned the laptop off, flipped it upside down, and tried to dry it as fast as we could. I was so worried that I could barely sleep that night. But luckily, the next morning, it turned on like nothing had happened. We both did pretty well on the exam too. Now Minji teases me about it every time we go there. So yeah, that's pretty much a day I'll never forget.

questions.en: How has the way you use cafes changed over the years? Compare how you used cafes in the past with how you use them now.
questions.ko: 카페를 이용하는 방식이 몇 년 사이 어떻게 달라졌나요? 예전과 지금의 카페 이용을 비교해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 예전(고등학생 때) → 지금(대학생) → 가장 큰 차이와 이유 → 마무리
목적(놀기 → 공부), 음료(달달한 음료 → 아이스 아메리카노), 시간(짧게 → 오래) 중 2~3개만 비교하세요
used to + 동사원형 / These days ~ 로 과거와 현재를 또렷하게 나누세요

answers.IM3: Sure, I'd love to talk about it. When I was in high school, I didn't go to cafes very often. I went there just to hang out with my friends. I usually ordered sweet drinks, like milk tea. Now I'm a college student, and I go to cafes to study. I go two or three times a week. I order an iced Americano because it helps me stay awake. Yeah, that's how it has changed.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about it. The way I use cafes has changed a lot. When I was in high school, I didn't go to cafes very often, because I was always busy studying at school or at an academy. When I did go, it was just to hang out with my friends on weekends. We used to order sweet drinks like milk tea or smoothies, and we chatted and took lots of pictures. Now I'm a college student, and cafes are basically my study room. I go two or three times a week, and I usually stay for two or three hours. I also drink iced Americanos now, because they help me stay awake. The biggest difference is the reason I go. Before, it was all about fun. Now it's more about getting work done. So yeah, that's how it has changed.
answers.AL: Sure, I'd love to talk about it, because it's changed a lot. Back in high school, I didn't really go to cafes that often. I was always busy studying, either at school or at an academy until late at night. So when I did go, it was usually on a weekend, just to hang out with my friends. We used to order super sweet drinks, like milk tea or strawberry smoothies, and we'd sit there chatting and taking a million pictures. We'd only stay for an hour or so. These days, it's a completely different story. Now that I'm a college student, cafes are basically my study room. I go two or three times a week, and I usually stay for two or three hours with my laptop. My taste has changed too. I hardly ever order sweet drinks anymore. I just get an iced Americano, because I need the caffeine to get through my assignments. I think the biggest change is the reason I go. In high school, it was all about having fun. Now it's more about having a quiet place to focus. But I still hang out with Minji there, so it's a bit of both. So yeah, that's pretty much how it's changed.

pronunciation.tip: 두 번째 음절 '페이'에 강세. '카페'처럼 평평하게 말하지 말고 '캐페이'에 가깝게
첫 음절 '앳'에 강세. 3음절로 '앳머스피어', 끝을 '스페어'로 하지 않기
미국식은 t가 약해져 '라아레이'에 가깝게. '라떼'처럼 된소리로 하지 않기
첫 음절 '레'에 강세. 가운데 '귤'은 약하게, 끝 r은 혀를 말아서
